Part 1

How much leaves, how fast, and in what form?

Part 1 · the plan

Five scenarios and their source terms

  1. The method chainsource, dispersion, effect, impact, severity
  2. Five credible eventsburst, slurry, hot feed, steam, magma spill
  3. Liquid through a holeCHEF eq. 12-5 and a hole lab
  4. Steam through a holechoked flow, eq. 12-4

Step 1 · interactive · pick a stage

Each stage takes the result of the one before

Dispersion and fire are short here: nothing burns and no toxic cloud forms.

Step 2 · interactive · pick a scenario

One credible event per hazard type

Inventories, pressures and temperatures come from the model at design: the screening moves with the plant.

Step 3 · CHEF eq. 12-5

A pressurised liquid leaks by Bernoulli

$$L = 1.1\,c_d\,d^2\sqrt{\rho_L\left[1000\,(P_0-P_A)+9.8\,\rho_L h'\right]}$$

1.1 ≈ $\tfrac{\pi}{4}\sqrt{2}$: the orifice equation with $P_0-P_A$ in kPa and a liquid head $h'$ in m.

S2: $P_0-P_A = 218.8$ kPa at the P-301 discharge, $d$ = 25 mmmodel vacuum + pump head
$L = 1.1\cdot0.61\cdot0.025^2\sqrt{1250\cdot1000\cdot218.8} = 6.9$ kg/sabout 25 t/h of 62 °C slurry

Step 3 · interactive · fines-loop leak S2

Hole size and time to stop set the spill

Liquid hole, eq. 12-5$L = 1.1\,c_d\,d^2\sqrt{1000\,\rho_L\,\Delta P}$
release, t/h
spilled, t
spray, m

Rate grows with $d^2$, the spill with the stop time: a remote stop of P-301 cuts the spill more than a smaller hole.

Step 4 · interactive · LP steam jet S4

Steam leaves at sonic speed: rate ∝ pressure

Choked when $P_A/P_0 < 0.528$, eq. 12-4$\dot m \propto c_d\,d^2\,P_0$
steam, kg/h
burns to, m

A 10 mm leak at 3.5 bar a puts out about 96 kg/h and burns within about 4 m: a fitter at the flange is the person at risk.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • Five scenarios: burst, slurry leak, hot-feed leak, steam jet, magma spill.
  • Liquid leaks by Bernoulli, $L \propto d^2\sqrt{\Delta P}$.
  • Steam chokes: the rate follows $P_0$, not the back pressure.
  • Plant limits (stop time, pump run-out) cap the spill.

The source is known. Next: how far its effects reach.

Part 2

How far do the blast, the spray and the steam reach?

Part 2 · the plan

Blast, scald and the reach of each effect

  1. Stored pressure energyeq. 14-1 and the TNT equivalent
  2. A burst laboverpressure against distance
  3. Scald timeseconds at 60 °C, instant at the boil
  4. Effect distancesinside the unit or beyond it

Step 1 · CHEF eq. 14-1

A burst releases the energy of the compressed vapour

$$E = P_B V\left[\ln\frac{P_B}{P_A} - \left(1-\frac{P_A}{P_B}\right)\right],\qquad W = \frac{E}{4690},\qquad X_{1\,\text{psi}} = 18\,W^{1/3}$$
S1: steam at 3.5 bar a fills $V$ = 71.5 m³ of vapour space (tube rupture, no relief)level 50 %, freeboard 1.5 m
$E$ = 13 240 kJ → $W$ = 2.8 kg TNT → 1 psi at 25 misothermal energy, as CHEF

The 60 °C magma does not flash at 1 atm, so only the vapour counts.

Step 2 · interactive · CR-201 burst S1

Burst pressure and vapour space set the blast

Blast, from step 1$W = E/4690,\ \ X_{1\,\text{psi}} = 18\,W^{1/3}$
kg TNT
1 psi, m
3 psi, m

At steam pressure 1 psi reaches 25 m; at the 1 bar g design pressure still 15 m: the relief device (R01) is what removes this case.

Step 3 · interactive · move the temperature

Hot water burns in seconds above 60 °C

s to a full-thickness scald

The fines loop at 62 °C scalds in under 4 s; the 120 °C feed at once: no one can step back in time.

Step 4 · interactive · pick a scenario

Which effects leave the unit?

Sprays and the steam jet stay inside 20 m; the burst and an unkerbed magma spill do not.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • A burst of CR-201 at steam pressure: 2.8 kg TNT, 1 psi at 25 m.
  • Hot liquor scalds in seconds; at the boil, at once.
  • Sprays and steam stay local; blast and spill reach beyond the unit.

The effects are mapped. Next: how many people they reach.

Part 3

How many people are hurt, and does the team's S agree?

Part 3 · the plan

Count people, then question the studies

  1. People and the RAST level$N = A\,\rho_{pop} + n_v$
  2. Sensitivitywhat moves the level
  3. Against HAZID and HAZOPsame or review
  4. Checked against CHEFthe workbook itself

Step 1 · interactive · who is standing there?

Severity counts people, not metres

CHEF impact rule$N = A\,\rho_{pop} + n_v$

With one person at the leak every scenario is level 4; with nobody it drops: occupancy drives the level more than physics.

Step 2 · interactive · pick a case

One input changed at a time

A kerb shrinks the spill; a remote stop shrinks the slurry release: plant changes move the result, not just assumptions.

Step 3 · interactive · pick a scenario

The screening beside the team's severity

"Review" is a question for the team, not a correction: the team judged a person at the leak; the screening counts one by default.

Step 4 · interactive · pick a scenario

Every number typed into the CHEF workbook

The engine reproduces the workbook cell by cell: a screening you can audit, not a black box.

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • $N = A\,\rho_{pop} + n_v$; the RAST level follows from $N$.
  • Who stands at the leak decides most levels.
  • Four of five scenarios ask the team to review its S.
  • The engine matches the CHEF workbook within 3 %.

The severity is set. Next: the Safety layers and LOPA tabs ask how often.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

A non-flammable salt still has hazards: stored pressure, heat and inventory.

2

Follow the chain: source, effect, impact, people, level.

3

Without a relief device, a burst of CR-201 reaches 25 m.

4

Use the screening to question the team's S, never to overwrite it.
